title: 住民に残る根強い不安　米艦載機の訓練、岩国基地が代替施設に
extracted_text: 在日米海軍が30日、米軍岩国基地（山口県岩国市）を拠点にする空母艦載機による陸上離着陸訓練（FCLP）を硫黄島（東京都）で実施すると発表したのを受け、県と岩国市などは国や米軍に対し、訓練を硫黄島で完了させ、岩国基地で実施しないよう要請した。住民からは根強い不安や懸念の声が上がった。 在日米海軍などによると、硫黄島での実施期間は7～17日。悪天候などで硫黄島で実施できない場合を想定し、岩国基地など四つの在日米軍基地を代替施設に指定し、12～17日実施する可能性があるとしている。 県と岩国市などは30日、岩国基地や中国四国防衛局（広島市）に担当者を派遣して訓練を硫黄島で完了し、今後は代替施設にも指定しないよう文書で要請。FCLP後に艦載機が洋上の空母で実施する空母着艦資格取得訓練（CQ）についても、艦載機が岩国基地に帰還することなく、硫黄島周辺で実施するよう口頭で申し入れた。 米軍機による騒音への損害賠償や飛行差し止めを求めている第2次岩国騒音訴訟の三木健二原告団長は「米軍機の爆音は、子どもや病人など弱者にとっては耐えがたい。昨年は地元の反対を押し切ってFCLPが強行され、住民は我慢するしかなかった。二度としてほしくないが、どうなるか分からないので、まだ不安だ」と話した。 基地機能強化に反対する「瀬戸内海の静かな環境を守る住民ネットワーク」の久米慶典共同代表は「岩国で実施されたFCLPは、受忍の限度を超える訓練であると認識された。今後、中東情勢の推移によっては、岩国基地で再び強行される恐れもある。米軍や国は、反対する住民の声を真摯（しんし）に受け止めるべきだ」と訴える。 岩国基地では2025年9月、約25年ぶりにFCLPが実施された。期間中、艦載機が滑走路に降下し、急上昇する「タッチ・アンド・ゴー」が繰り返され、市に寄せられた騒音などの苦情は1000件を超えた。訓練は予定時間を超えて連日続き、事前通告に反して祝日の訓練もあり、県や市は岩国基地で実施ないよう国に求めていた。【大山典男】
translated_text: In response to the announcement on the 30th by the U.S. Navy in Japan that carrier-based aircraft Field Carrier Landing Practice (FCLP) will be conducted at Iwo Jima (Tokyo Metropolis), the prefecture and Iwakuni City requested the national government and the U.S. military to complete the training at Iwo Jima and not to conduct it at Iwakuni Base. Residents voiced deep-seated anxiety and concerns. According to the U.S. Navy in Japan, the training at Iwo Jima is scheduled for the 7th through the 17th. To account for cases where training cannot be conducted at Iwo Jima due to bad weather, four U.S. military bases in Japan, including Iwakuni Base, have been designated as alternative facilities, with training potentially conducted from the 12th through the 17th. On the 30th, the prefecture and Iwakuni City dispatched officials to Iwakuni Base and the Chugoku-Shikoku Regional Defense Bureau (in Hiroshima City) to formally request that training be completed at Iwo Jima and that the base not be designated as an alternative facility in the future. They also verbally requested that Carrier Qualification (CQ) training, conducted over the ocean on carriers after FCLP, be conducted near Iwo Jima without the carrier aircraft returning to Iwakuni Base. Kenji Miki, lead plaintiff in the second Iwakuni noise lawsuit seeking compensation for noise damage and an injunction against military aircraft operations, said: "The deafening noise from U.S. military aircraft is unbearable for vulnerable people like children and the sick. Last year, FCLP was pushed through despite local opposition, and residents had no choice but to endure it. I don't want it to happen again, but I don't know what's going to happen, so I'm still anxious." Keiten Kume, co-representative of the Residents' Network to Protect the Quiet Environment of the Seto Inland Sea, which opposes the strengthening of base functions, stated: "It was recognized that the FCLP conducted at Iwakuni exceeded the limits of acceptable忍耐 [endurance]. Depending on how the Middle East situation develops, there is a risk that training could be forced through again at Iwakuni Base. The U.S. military and the government should sincerely heed the voices of residents who oppose this." FCLP was conducted at Iwakuni Base in September 2025 for the first time in about 25 years. During the training period, carrier aircraft repeatedly performed touch-and-go maneuvers — descending and then rapidly climbing from the runway — and the city received over 1,000 complaints about noise and other issues. Training continued daily beyond the scheduled hours, including on holidays despite prior notice, and the prefecture and city had requested the national government that training not be conducted at Iwakuni Base. [Norio Oyama]
title_en: Persistent anxiety remains among residents — US carrier aircraft training, Iwakuni Base designated as backup facility
